purpose: Reusable, independently addressable desired outcomes, initially 19 candidates without claiming proven atomicity.

candidates.definition: Acknowledge successful preceding work without causing an unnecessary handoff.
Resume current project work instead of initiating an unrelated objective.
Advance as much legitimate in-scope work as available execution permits.
Advance toward the originally defined, verifiable acceptance target.
Recover established decisions, constraints, roadmap and known progress.
Identify and resume incomplete work after an interruption.
Base decisions on available repository, test and deliverable evidence.
Explain what happened, what remains, and what is uncertain.
Identify/prioritize the next legitimate unfinished requirement.
Implement, test and commit actual deliverables across execution cycles.
Do not duplicate finished work or assume an interrupted action succeeded.
Avoid unauthorized features, tasks or goal substitutions.
Avoid repetitive planning, cosmetic busywork and performance theater.
Compare reported achievements against evidence and acceptance criteria.
Correct invented, overstated or repetitive progress assertions.
Report a verifiable completion percentage and change where measurable.
Continue other legitimate tasks when one requirement is blocked.
Avoid premature termination and stop on validated completion or true execution exhaustion.
At the appropriate boundary, report tangible changes, blockers, and remaining work.

design_constraints: No prompt is created for each intent by queueing.
Separate goals from constraints, stop conditions, reporting requirements, and methods.
Descriptions are public-safe, neutral summaries rather than private conversation excerpts.
open_review_questions: Which items are genuinely atomic versus procedural requirements?
Which intents are version-specific rather than shared by all generations?
